subject: Staged overrun guardrail and procurement path for launch week
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@cartwheellabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cartwheellabs.com
Date: 2028-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch week capacity ask + overrun mechanics

Hi Ben,

Quick note from our side — we go live with Cartwheel v2 next Tuesday and expect an unpredictable traffic spike (beta users + promo). Our infra team flagged that the current quota will likely be exhausted within hours under an optimistic forecast.

We need a short-term plan that: 1) prevents hard throttling during the launch window, 2) keeps cost predictable for our CFO, and 3) aligns with our procurement cadence (we need a PO-ready quote by EOD Wednesday).

Questions:
- Can Redwood open a temporary burst pool (2–3x our committed QPS) for a 72-hour window?
- How will overrun billing be handled — immediate invoice versus true-up on monthly invoice?
- Any one-off discounts or credits for startup launches?

If it helps, I can share traffic forecasts and the launch timeline. Procurement is CC'd — they want a clear commercial attachment to sign.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Martinez
Head of Product
Cartwheel Labs
Elena mobile: +1 415 555 0138
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@cartwheellabs.com>
Cc: procurement@cartwheellabs.com
Date: 2028-07-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask + overrun mechanics

Elena — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch. We can absolutely help avoid a hard throttle during the window. High level proposal below; attaching a provisional schedule and a one-page quote for PO prep.

Proposal (72-hr launch window):
- Temporary burst pool: up to 2.5x committed QPS, pre-warmed. Activated on request and monitored by our SREs.
- Billing mechanics: overrun will be invoiced as a provisional charge at the time of the event (to cover immediate capacity costs) and then true-up on the next monthly invoice to reflect final token counts — with a reconciliation line that nets provisional payment.
- Discount: 20% credit on overrun token unit price applied once monthly true-up shows cumulative overrun < 200% of committed volume. If overrun exceeds that, we reduce the credit to 10% for the portion above 200%. This is a temporary launch concession.
- PO-ready materials: CW-quote-20280722.xlsx and CW-provisional-burst-schedule-20280722.pdf attached.

Operational asks from Cartwheel:
- Provide an hourly forecast CSV (peak 48 hours ahead would be ideal).
- A point of contact for on-call escalation during the window.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll loop in Laura (finance) to confirm invoicing language and Connor (CS) to arrange SRE coverage.

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (650) 555-0199
From: Elena Martinez <elena@cartwheellabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cartwheellabs.com
Date: 2028-07-22T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask + overrun mechanics

Ben — this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. A few clarifications:

1) The CFO is nervous about provisional charges being non-refundable if the true-up reduces the total — can you confirm the provisional will always be credited back (not forfeited) if the monthly reconciliation shows lower usage?
2) Can the provisional payment be capped to a dollar ceiling (we propose $50k) to keep runway predictable?
3) Is the 20% credit applied to unit overrun price or the provisional invoice amount?

Procurement note: we can issue a PO quickly once the XLS shows a clean line item for the 72-hour burst and a PO reference field.

I’ll attach our traffic forecast in a follow-up within the hour.

Thanks,
Elena
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@cartwheellabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, procurement@cartwheellabs.com
Date: 2028-07-22T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask + overrun mechanics

Hi Elena — Laura here from Finance, looping in Connor for operational coordination. Thanks for the forecast — that helped. We can put the commercial terms into PO-ready language: 

1) Provisional charge behavior: any provisional payments are held as credits on the Cartwheel account. If the monthly true-up calculates a lower final charge, the provisional credit will be applied to the invoice and any remainder will be refunded or offset against the next month per your preference.

2) Cap: we can set a provisional cap of $50,000 for the 72-hour window as requested. If usage suggests a breach, we'll contact the Cartwheel POC and open an emergency approval path rather than auto-raise the cap.

3) Credit mechanics: the 20% launch credit applies to the final overrun unit price on the monthly reconciliation (i.e., credit applied at true-up, not at provisional invoice). For clarity in the XLS we have a line called "Estimated provisional charge" and a separate "Estimated true-up credit" line.

Next steps:
- Ben will send an updated XLS with a PO line and a PO reference field populated.
- Connor will coordinate SRE pre-warm and on-call schedule.
- Procurement: if you can return a signed PO referencing DEAL-1872 by 2028-07-23 17:00 PDT, we will lock the burst window and SRE staffing.

Attachments included here are the final quote and schedule (same filenames Ben attached).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
